bundle.meaning: Path to a readable CA-only certificate bundle. PEM platforms require one certificate; Windows selects DER.

platform.meaning: Platform selecting bundle encoding, defaulting to linux when omitted.

fingerprint.meaning: Optional exact match to the supplied bundle fingerprint; required on first contact without a local or recorded root pin. It does not override a local root pin.

renew-ring.meaning: Permit replacing a different ledger pin, but not a different local CA pin.

dry-run.meaning: Validate the bundle and pin, then report prospective trust and ledger effects without applying them.

primitive.meaning: The certificate operation (trust_install), or error for the stop-level exception arm.

role.meaning: Normalized appliance profile used by the certificate operation.

changed.meaning: Whether the primitive reports a change; some failure paths may report partial effects.

dry_run.meaning: Whether the primitive returned a dry-run receipt; a refusal before planning can report false.

state_generation.meaning: Reported generation of the certificate state, or 0 when not available.

client_reinstall_required.meaning: Whether clients must reinstall trust for the reported operation.

platform.meaning: Platform selecting the exported CA bundle encoding and filename.

ca_fingerprint.meaning: SHA-256 fingerprint reported for the House CA certificate.

bundle_fingerprint.meaning: Fingerprint of the supplied CA bundle, null on a bundle validation failure.

supplied_fingerprint.meaning: Fingerprint read from the supplied certificate during pin validation.

caller_fingerprint.meaning: Provided fingerprint echoed on a caller mismatch, including invalid types.

reason.meaning: Pin, trust-store or ledger disposition accompanying the outcome.

pin_decision.meaning: How the active root fingerprint was selected or why it was refused.

pin_sources.meaning: Available local certificate and state ledger pin sources.

bundle_installed.meaning: Whether the certificate is installed and was read back in system trust.

anchor_path.meaning: Path of the platform trust anchor.

system_bundle.meaning: Path of the system bundle checked for trust.

detail.meaning: Ledger read or parse diagnostic when available.

refresh_program.meaning: Platform trust refresh program selected by the plan.

refresh_command.meaning: Trust refresh argument vector in the plan.

refresh_available.meaning: Whether the planned trust refresh tool was found.

would_write_anchor.meaning: Whether the plan would write the platform anchor.

would_refresh.meaning: Whether the plan would refresh system trust.

would_commit_state.meaning: Whether the plan would change the trust ledger.

would_bridge.meaning: Whether the plan would bridge browser trust.

plan.meaning: Ordered action names describing the proposed operation.

store_refresh.meaning: Refresh program, argv, exit status or null, and attempt or error facts as available.

state_commit.meaning: Ledger update child receipt, or null if no write was needed.

browser_trust.meaning: Browser bridge verdict; null when not applicable and unsupported for a missing bridge.

bridge.meaning: Browser bridge state before the operation, whether attempted, and exit status or null.

proof.meaning: Evidence named by the primitive for this outcome.

firstMissingSignal.meaning: Outcome token; none on success. The stop also passes through raw validation, tool and filesystem exception text on some paths; those diagnostics are not fixed tokens.
